svg.title: Example with made-up inputs: merino at $0.75 a wear and synthetic at $0.90
svg.desc: Example with made-up inputs. A merino top at $90 worn 120 times costs $0.75 a wear. A synthetic top at $36 worn 40 times costs $0.90 a wear. The bars are different lengths. Not shelf prices.
svg.text: Example with made-up inputs: cost per wear
Price divided by wears. Not a shelf price and not a wear test.
$90 / 120 = $0.75. The lower bar is the lower cost per wear.
$36 / 40 = $0.90. It is higher per wear because it is worn less often
in this example, not because synthetic is a worse fibre.
If you will not wear the merino top 120 times, do not use $0.75.
Saving Optimizer. Example with made-up inputs. Checked 29 Sep 2026.
